Hi Dev,

Thanks for taking this — we pulled our May usage and there’s a sharp spike in the week of May 9–15 that pushed us well above our committed capacity. We were in the middle of a data migration that unfortunately hit a few large backfills; the attached CSV is the raw token/hour breakdown.

Hi Elise — thanks for the data and the quick heads up. I’m looping Laura from billing to make sure the math and invoice path are straight.

Summary of what we saw (preliminary): the migration burst on May 11–13 created ~1.2M extra tokens beyond your committed capacity for May. Using your committed price tier (Reserved Capacity Q3 discount applied), that maps to a gross overage of $38,450. I attached a short proforma workbook showing the line-by-line calculation and the hourly breakdown we derived from your CSV.

Settlement paths we can do (pick one):
- One-time invoice (Net 30) for the full $38,450 — we issue a single invoice and you pay per normal AP process.
- Apply a credit across your next renewal term (we can amortize across the 12-month renewal).
- Staged payment: 50% up front / 50% in 30 days — we can do this and add a small administrative hold until fully paid.

We can also offer a 5% goodwill credit on the overage amount if BrightForge agrees to a firm PO and payment schedule this week — that would reduce the net to $36,527.50. No obligations on future scaling; we’ll add a recommended autoscale cap and alerting playbook to avoid surprises moving forward.

Next steps I propose: you confirm preferred settlement path and PO cadence; if you accept the staged payment + goodwill credit option, I’ll route to Laura to generate a final invoice and to Finance for payment instructions.

Attaching: redwood_proforma_DF-2719.xlsx

Best,
